# FEATURE: Parser Keys

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Parses TOML bare, quoted, and dotted keys with correct definition semantics. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Boundaries.md |
| Provides    | bare keys, quoted keys, dotted keys, nested document paths, duplicate-key rejection |
| Consumes    | stdin TOML decoder, TOML lexical parsers |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Support TOML key forms and map key/value assignments into nested JSON objects.

## Behavior

- Accept bare keys containing ASCII letters, digits, underscores, and dashes.
- Accept basic-string and literal-string quoted keys, including empty quoted keys.
- Accept dotted keys with whitespace around components.
- Create implicit tables for dotted paths.
- Treat quoted and bare spellings of the same key as equivalent.
- Reject duplicate keys and attempts to extend scalar or inline-table values as tables.
- Preserve numeric-looking bare keys as string keys.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC parser-keys-conformance ===
Intent: The implementation passes the complete authoritative key conformance slice.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/stage_test.sh", "valid/key/**|invalid/key/**"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC parser-keys-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not accept duplicate or conflicting key definitions.
- Do not reinterpret numeric-looking bare keys as numeric values.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Parser Tables

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Parses standard tables and arrays of tables with TOML definition and targeting rules. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Parser-Keys.md |
| Provides    | standard table headers, array-of-table headers, table targeting and redefinition validation |
| Consumes    | stdin TOML decoder, dotted key document paths |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Support table headers and arrays of tables while preserving TOML ordering and redefinition semantics.

## Behavior

- Parse standard table headers with bare, quoted, and dotted names.
- Create implicit parent tables where permitted.
- Reject duplicate table definitions and table/scalar conflicts.
- Parse arrays of tables and append elements in source order.
- Target the most recently defined array element for nested tables and arrays.
- Reject child definitions whose array parent has not yet been established.
- Reject attempts to append to ordinary arrays or redefine tables as arrays.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC parser-tables-conformance ===
Intent: The implementation passes the complete authoritative table conformance slice.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/stage_test.sh", "valid/table/**|invalid/table/**"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC parser-tables-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Preserve array-of-table element order.
- Reject table redefinitions and invalid table/array conflicts.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Parser-Arrays-Inline.md ===
# FEATURE: Parser Arrays and Inline Tables

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Parses TOML arrays and closed inline tables, including nested and mixed values. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Parser-Keys.md |
| Provides    | TOML arrays, nested arrays, mixed values, inline tables, inline-table closure |
| Consumes    | stdin TOML decoder, TOML key parser, TOML scalar and string parsers |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Implement TOML array and inline-table values with their nesting, whitespace, comment, and closure rules.

## Behavior

- Parse empty, single-line, multiline, nested, and mixed-type arrays.
- Permit comments and trailing commas in arrays.
- Parse inline tables containing all supported TOML value types.
- Support nested inline tables and dotted keys inside inline tables.
- Reject trailing commas and newlines that are not valid within inline-table values.
- Reject attempts to extend an inline table after its closing brace.
- Preserve array element order and tagged value types.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC parser-arrays-inline-conformance ===
Intent: The implementation passes the complete authoritative array and inline-table conformance slice.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/stage_test.sh", "valid/array/**|valid/inline-table/**|invalid/array/**|invalid/inline-table/**"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC parser-arrays-inline-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not allow inline tables to be extended after closure.
- Do not accept trailing commas in inline tables.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Parser Datetimes

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Parses TOML offset and local date/time values into tagged representations. |
| Depends On  | FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Boundaries.md |
| Provides    | offset datetime, local datetime, local date, and local time values |
| Consumes    | stdin TOML decoder, tagged JSON output |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Recognize TOML v1.0.0 date and time forms and serialize them using the decoder's required tagged JSON representation.

## Behavior

- Parse RFC 3339 offset datetimes with `Z` and numeric offsets.
- Parse local datetimes without an offset.
- Parse local dates and local times.
- Accept permitted fractional seconds and truncate unsupported precision rather than round.
- Reject malformed dates, times, offsets, and invalid local forms.
- Emit the types `datetime`, `datetime-local`, `date-local`, and `time-local`.
- Serialize values as the required RFC 3339 or date/time strings.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC parser-datetimes-conformance ===
Intent: The implementation passes the complete authoritative date/time conformance slice.
Suite: scoped
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        "sh",
        "sources/stage_test.sh",
        "valid/datetime/**|invalid/datetime/**|invalid/local-date/**|invalid/local-datetime/**|invalid/local-time/**",
    ],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC parser-datetimes-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not attach local date/time values to an implicit timezone.
- Truncate excess fractional precision; never round it.
=== END ARTIFACT ===

# FEATURE: Complete Conformance Verification

| Field       | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| Version     | 20260815 V1 |
| Description | Verifies the completed decoder against the complete supplied TOML v1.0.0 conformance suite. |
| Depends On  | ARCHITECTURE.md, FEATURE-Decoder-Contract.md, FEATURE-Parser-Strings.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Scalars.md, FEATURE-Parser-Lexical-Boundaries.md, FEATURE-Parser-Parser-Keys.md, FEATURE-Parser-Tables.md, FEATURE-Parser-Arrays-Inline.md, FEATURE-Parser-Datetimes.md |
| Provides    | complete TOML v1.0.0 conformance verdict |
| Consumes    | completed stdin TOML decoder |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose

Provide the terminal, unfiltered verification of the complete TOML parser implementation.

## Verification

- Build the fixed `cmd/toml-decoder` entry point.
- Run the supplied `sources/full_test.sh` command without filtering or reinterpretation.
- Require the authoritative `toml-test` v2.2.0 suite to exit successfully.
- Treat the suite exit status as the complete release verification result.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC complete-conformance ===
Intent: The completed implementation passes the complete authoritative TOML v1.0.0 conformance suite.
Suite: full
Requires: executable=go; scope=test
Requires: executable=toml-test; scope=test

import subprocess

result = subprocess.run(
    ["sh", "sources/full_test.sh"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)
print(result.stderr)
assert result.returncode == 0
=== END AC complete-conformance ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not filter, skip, reinterpret, or replace the complete conformance verdict.
- Do not assert or depend on a fixed case count.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
